haiku-low.q1: Probes seeing 3 consecutive /healthz failures from 2 of 3 locations page on-call, which takes no automatic action. A person runs the single failover command.
haiku-low.q2: If B's last recorded replay lag is over 30 s, the command stops with nothing changed, unless the operator passes the accept-data-loss override, which is recorded.
haiku-low.q3: Promotion needs the fence wait (35 s) finished. Workers need B_PROMOTED recorded and the requeue done. DNS needs the B app health check passing, including a database write probe.
haiku-low.q4: B's Redis starts empty, so every signed-in user must sign in again. Expect a login spike right after DNS moves.
haiku-low.q5: It stays read-only until rebuilt as a replica of B. It is never reused as primary. Failing back is a separate planned switchover.
haiku-low.q6: A's lease agent renews its write lease only while the record says active=A. Once renewals stop, the 30 s lease expires and A's database goes read-only and stops Postgres. The command waits 35 s before promoting B.
haiku-low.q7: The active-region record, a strongly consistent store outside both regions. The command writes it for lock, fence and resume. A's lease agent reads and renews it. Restarted A reads it.
haiku-low.q8: Rows left running in A are copied to B as running, then set to pending in one transaction before B's workers start. Jobs are at-least-once, so handlers need idempotency keys.
haiku-low.q9: Rerun the same command; it reads the record and resumes at the first incomplete step. Going back to A needs a human to deliberately set active=A with a new epoch. The command never does this.
haiku-low.q10: NOT STATED for connection behavior during failover. The plan says traffic reaches B within the 60 s DNS TTL, and users must sign in again.
haiku-low.q11: Data committed in A's final unreplicated WAL is lost; the target RPO is 30 s. The lag check blocks failover over 30 s unless overridden. Lag can understate loss.

sonnet.q1: A person (on-call) running the single failover command starts it. Detection (2 of 3 probe locations see 3 consecutive /healthz failures) only pages on-call; no automatic action.
sonnet.q2: If B's last recorded replay lag is over 30 s, the command stops with nothing changed and A still active, unless the operator passes the accept-data-loss override. With the override, it records that in the run field and continues.
sonnet.q3: Before promoting B's DB: the record is CAS'd to FENCING (epoch+1, active=B), A's lease renewals have stopped, and the 35 s wait (30 s TTL + 5 s margin) has finished. Before B's workers start: B_PROMOTED recorded (DB verified writable) and the requeue transaction set running jobs to pending (unless skipped by the requeued/workers_started flag). Before DNS points at B: B_PROMOTED, app scaled up, and the B app health check (including a DB write probe) passed.
sonnet.q4: Sessions are lost. B's Redis starts empty, so every signed-in user must sign in again, and a login spike is expected after DNS moves.
sonnet.q5: Once the record leaves A_ACTIVE, a returning A cannot take writes and stays read-only until it is rebuilt as a replica of B. The old A database is never reused as primary. Failing back is a separate planned switchover with its own plan.
sonnet.q6: The lease fence. A's lease agent renews a 30 s write lease only while the record says active=A. A partitioned A cannot reach the record, so it cannot renew. Its database goes read-only and Postgres is stopped when the lease runs out, with a local watchdog if the agent hangs. The command waits 35 s before promoting B. A restarted A comes up read-only and takes writes only after reading active=A.
sonnet.q7: The active-region record, a new strongly consistent key-value store outside both regions that supports CAS and leases. The failover command writes it (CAS to FENCING, B_PROMOTED, B_ACTIVE, run flags) and reads it at every step to resume. A's lease agent reads it and renews against it.
sonnet.q8: Rows that were running are copied to B as running. After promotion and before B's workers start, one transaction sets all running rows to pending, so the jobs are rerun (at-least-once). It is skipped on rerun if requeued or workers_started is set. Job handlers with side effects need idempotency keys. Jobs enqueued or completed in the final unreplicated WAL are lost.
sonnet.q9: Rerun the same idempotent command. It reads the record and resumes at the first incomplete step. Going back to A is possible only if B's database cannot be made writable (state FENCING, promotion failing). A's data is intact, and only a human can deliberately move the record back to active=A with a new epoch. After B_PROMOTED it only rolls forward; the command never demotes B.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED for what the client itself experiences. The document says only that traffic reaches B within the 60 s DNS TTL, that A is fenced, and that users see A's outage until DNS moves.
sonnet.q11: Up to the final unreplicated WAL, the RPO window of 30 s. The lag check (over 30 s needs the override) is the limit. The lag value is stale because it freezes when A dies, so passing the check does not guarantee the RPO was met. The command should print the last WAL receipt time.
